title: Variance-estimator-induced provisioning oscillation and cold-start reduction plan
creator: Lena Park
description: Summary: A regression in the autoscaler metric aggregation introduced high-frequency oscillation in provisioned replica counts for latency-sensitive inference pools. The metric estimator began amplifying transient latency spikes, causing repeated scale-ups that were followed by aggressive scale-downs; the churn increased cold-starts and P95 tail latency for several hosted routes. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, short-term mitigations applied, and the longer-term action plan to make the autoscaler robust to high-variance traffic patterns.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-20 02:47 UTC - First customer alert: elevated P95 latency for text-generation-prod-route-7 via monitoring.
2026-02-20 03:10 UTC - Automation triggered scale-up to burst pool; observed increased replica churn over next 18 minutes.
2026-02-20 03:29 UTC - Several requests saw cold-start latency > 1.8s; error rates remained low but increased user-observed tail latency.
2026-02-20 03:45 UTC - On-call ran temporary stabilization: cap autoscaler to +40% over baseline and enabled a 5m hold window for downscales.
2026-02-20 05:00 UTC - Traffic returned to baseline; manual rollback of temporary caps at 05:40 after confirming mitigations.
2026-02-20 10:00 UTC - Initial RCA meeting; assigned investigation owners and data owners for metric pipelines.
root_cause: A recent change to the percentile estimator in the autoscaler metrics pipeline (migrating from a reservoir-based sampler to a sliding-window P95 estimator with naive weighting) made brief latency blips count disproportionately in the configured percentiles. Combined with aggressive scale-down configuration (short stabilization window and narrow hysteresis), this caused the control loop to treat noise as signal, resulting in oscillatory provisioning. The KEDA scaler mapping for coldpool targets also lacked a minimum steady-state guard, amplifying drop-to-zero behavior when traffic momentarily subsided.
mitigation_during_incident: Applied temporary scale cap: limited scale-up to +40% of baseline for affected pools (rollbackable).
Increased downscale stabilization to 5m to reduce immediate tear-downs after spikes.
Enabled minimal warm-pool allocation for the most-sensitive routes (allocated 2 warm replicas per shard).
Deployed a hotfix to revert percentile estimator change in metrics pipeline while we design a robust aggregation approach.
Notified affected customers with summary and expected remediation ETA via status.redwood.ai post.
Opened an incident bridge and added targeted Grafana alerts for oscillation frequency and cold-start rate.
long_term_mitigations: Replace naive sliding-window P95 with a hybrid estimator: trimmed-quantile fusion that ignores transient top 2% anomalies and applies exponential smoothing across windows.
Introduce a request-class bucketing layer so autoscaler aggregates latency per request class (short, medium, long) to avoid mixing heterogeneous tails.
Implement a downscale hysteresis that considers both absolute delta and minimum replica floor per pool for at least 10 minutes after a scale event.

Add a KEDA mapping change: enforce minimum active replica floor when traffic exceeds a 1-min moving average, and add a secondary scale signal based on queue depth to avoid zeroing out under short pauses.
Add a warm-pool health probe so warm replicas can be reused without full startup cost and ensure warm-pool sizing suggestions are surfaced in Console Optimize.
Expand SLO monitoring: surface oscillation-rate metric on per-customer dashboards and add regression alert if oscillation frequency > 3 events/hour over 15m window.
